The most likely buggy method is `com.google.javascript.jscomp.CommandLineRunner.createOptions()`.

Why this is the best diagnosis:
- The failing behavior is that `--process_closure_primitives=false` does not disable Closure primitive rewriting.
- `DefaultPassConfig.getChecks()` only runs `ProcessClosurePrimitives` when `options.closurePass` is `true`.
- `CommandLineRunner.createOptions()` does this in the wrong direction:
  - It first calls `level.setOptionsForCompilationLevel(options)`.
  - For `SIMPLE_OPTIMIZATIONS`, that compilation-level setup sets `options.closurePass = true`.
  - It then only applies the flag with:
    ```java
    if (flags.process_closure_primitives) {
      options.closurePass = true;
    }
    ```
- That means the flag can enable the pass, but it cannot disable it. If the compilation level already enabled `closurePass`, passing `false` leaves it enabled.

Static evidence:
- `CommandLineRunner.createOptions()` lines 422-435 set compilation-level options before the conditional flag assignment.
- `CompilationLevel.applySafeCompilationOptions(...)` line 94 sets `options.closurePass = true`.
- `DefaultPassConfig.getChecks()` lines 188-198 gate Closure primitive passes on `options.closurePass`.

Dynamic evidence was only partial:
- It confirmed that compilation-level setup turns `options.closurePass` from `false` to `true` under `SIMPLE_OPTIMIZATIONS`.
- It did not capture the exact failing execution with the flag observed as `false`, so there is still a secondary possibility that boolean flag parsing is also involved.
- Even so, `createOptions()` is still incorrect as written because it does not honor an explicit `false` override.

Expected fix direction:
- In `createOptions()`, assign `options.closurePass = flags.process_closure_primitives;` after compilation-level setup, instead of only setting it when true.
